title: FIRST HOME BUYER GUIDE: GRANTS & TIPS FOR 2026
author: Finnova Financial Inclusion Team
excerpt: Buying your first home is an exciting milestone. Learn about the First Home Owner Grant (FHOG), stamp duty concessions, 5% deposit schemes, and securing competitive loan rates in 2026.
body:
💡 Executive Summary & Key Takeaways

In 2026, eligible Australian first home buyers can access direct capital grants up to $30,000, full stamp duty waivers, and the Federal Home Guarantee Scheme allowing purchases with only a 5% deposit without paying Lender's Mortgage Insurance (LMI).
1. 2026 State-by-State Grant & Duty Concession Breakdown
Government assistance programs vary significantly depending on which state or territory you reside in. Below is a comprehensive comparison of active incentives for 2026:

State / TerritoryFirst Home Owner Grant (FHOG)Full Stamp Duty Exemption ThresholdConcession Threshold
Victoria (VIC)$10,000 (New builds under $750k)Up to $600,000$600,001 – $750,000
New South Wales (NSW)$10,000 (New builds under $750k)Up to $800,000$800,001 – $1,000,000
Queensland (QLD)$30,000 (New builds under $750k)Up to $700,000$700,001 – $800,000
Western Australia (WA)$10,000 (New builds under $750k)Up to $450,000$450,001 – $600,000
2. The Federal Home Guarantee Scheme (5% Deposit, No LMI)

Under traditional lending criteria, purchasing a home with less than a 20% deposit requires paying Lender's Mortgage Insurance (LMI) — an upfront cost ranging from $15,000 to $35,000. However, through Housing Australia's First Home Guarantee (FHBG), eligible buyers can secure a home loan with as little as a 5% deposit while the Federal Government guarantees up to 15% of the loan value.

📌 Key Eligibility Requirements for the 5% Deposit Scheme:

  • Must be an Australian citizen or Permanent Resident aged 18+.
  • Income cap: Single applicants up to $125,000 per annum; Joint applicants up to $200,000 per annum.
  • Property price caps: Greater Melbourne ($800,000), Regional Victoria ($650,000), Sydney ($900,000), Brisbane ($700,000).
  • Must be an owner-occupier residential property (not an investment).
3. Step-by-Step Purchasing Roadmap for 2026

1

Credit Audit & Savings Benchmark

Ensure 3–6 months of clean bank statements, eliminate credit card limits, and demonstrate genuine savings equal to at least 5% of your target purchase price.

2

Pre-Approval with Accredited Lender

Work with an accredited broker or financial counselor to submit formal pre-approval applications and lock in home guarantee allocation spots.

3

Conveyancing & Settlement Assistance

Engage a licensed conveyancer or solicitor to review Section 32 vendor statements, verify title details, and process government grant applications prior to settlement.
4. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

❓ Can I claim the FHOG on an existing established house?

In most states including Victoria and NSW, the First Home Owner Grant ($10,000) applies exclusively to newly constructed homes, off-the-plan apartments, or substantially renovated properties. However, established homes are still eligible for full or partial stamp duty exemptions.

title: SMSF PROPERTY INVESTMENT: GROW YOUR SUPER
author: Finnova Wealth Team
excerpt: Take control of your retirement savings by investing in commercial or residential real estate through your self-managed super fund with Limited Recourse Borrowing Arrangements.
body:
💡 Executive Summary

Investing in real estate through a Self-Managed Super Fund (SMSF) offers unique tax concessions, including a maximum 15% tax rate on rental income and 0% Capital Gains Tax in the pension phase.
1. SMSF Property vs Personal Investment Comparison

FeatureSMSF Real Estate InvestmentPersonal Property Investment
Rental Income Tax RateMax 15% (0% in Pension Phase)Marginal Tax Rate (Up to 47%)
Capital Gains Tax (CGT)10% (If held >12 months; 0% in Pension)Up to 23.5% (with 50% discount)
Borrowing MechanismLimited Recourse Borrowing (LRBA)Standard Full Recourse Mortgage
Asset ProtectionProtected from personal bankruptcyExposed to personal creditor claims
2. ATO Compliance Rules for SMSF Property
The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) enforces strict governance around SMSF property transactions:

• Sole Purpose Test: The property must be acquired for the sole purpose of providing retirement benefits for fund members.
  • No Related Party Residential Leases: Neither SMSF trustees nor their family members may reside in or rent a residential property owned by the SMSF.
  • Commercial Property Exception: Business owners can lease commercial premises owned by their SMSF provided rent is paid at market rate.
